title: Predators with heritable 20-bit matching genotypes keep producing adaptive new genotypes without saturating: late shadow-calibrated cohort novelty 11-21 vs 1-2 in the in-world neutral twin (6/6 seeds), 12-56 vs 0-1 in a shuffled-genotype twin (4/4 valid seeds), 84 vs 7 over 700k steps (~900 predator generations) with a linear cumulative curve; prey stay at the neutral rate, and against Rechtsteiner-Bedau shadows the predator excess is only marginal
summary: Follow-up to 20261026T0605-c38-coev-matching-o, whose 2-D matching traits let prey escape. Here prey and predator traits are 20-bit genotypes in the same particle world, capture success exp(-h^2/w^2) on the Hamming distance h with w = 10 bits, so the space is finite (no escape to infinity) and predators keep a selection gradient everywhere. Kinds are exact genotypes; c30's o_measure counts late (t >= 20000) genotypes whose births within Lc = 10000 steps of their appearance exceed the 99.9th percentile of the same activity in a neutral reference. Predators: real 16, 11, 16, 21, 20, 19 vs 2, 2, 2, 2, 1, 2 in the constant-capture twin; real 51, 12, 27, 56 vs 0, 0, 1, 0 in the shuffled twin, where each attack uses a random predator's genotype (realised capture 0.09-0.12 there vs 0.22-0.26 with the attacker's own genotype, which is itself the evidence that predators are matched to the prey they meet); the 700k-step run gives 84 vs 7, at a constant rate to the end (figs/b10_summary.png). Predator births show recurrent sweeps (dominant genotype at 40-55% of births again and again, figs/b10L_s0_bits.png), the top-20 genotypes share nothing with the first window after t~40000, and 125 successive dominant genotypes return only 14 times in 700k steps. Prey are near neutral (19-33 vs 20-22). Against 8-16 Rechtsteiner-Bedau shadows the predator excess is marginal: above the shadow maximum at Lc = 10000 with 8 shadows in 3/3 seeds (7, 4, 9 vs max 3, 2, 4) but only in 2/3 seeds at Lc = 5000 and 1/3 at Lc = 20000 with 16 shadows, and prey fall below the shadows.

finding.operator: correlated matching between heritable bit-string genotypes of two coevolving, individually reproducing species (capture exp(-h^2/w^2) on Hamming distance, w = 10 of 20 bits)
finding.control: per seed: in-world neutral twin (constant capture = the real run's realised mean) and shuffled twin (attack success computed with a random living predator's genotype); a* = 99.9th percentile of the twin's early activity (o_measure.report with the twin as reference); also 8-16 Rechtsteiner-Bedau shadows at Lc = 5000, 10000, 20000
finding.result: late significant new predator genotypes real vs neutral twin 16/2, 11/2, 16/2, 21/2, 20/1, 19/2 (seeds 0-5); vs shuffled twin 51/0, 12/0, 27/1, 56/0 (seeds 0-3; seeds 4-5 invalid: the shuffled twin's predators died out, a* fell to 14 and 97); 700k-step run 84/7. Prey vs neutral twin 22/20, 28/21, 33/20, 19/22, 26/22, 29/20; long run 117/82. RB shadows, predators: Lc 10k (8 shadows) 7, 4, 9 vs ranges 0-3, 1-2, 0-4; Lc 5k (16) 5, 5, 4 vs max 3, 4, 5; Lc 20k (16) 2, 5, 8 vs max 2, 7, 6.

recommendation: This is the first world in the ledger whose late adaptive novelty stays above an in-world neutral twin for the whole run, and it does so through the mechanism c30's question predicted: a moving target made by another evolving population, with correlated (smooth) interaction in a heritable space the target cannot escape. Before anyone claims C:open-ended from it: (1) settle the reference: the RB shadow (well mixed) drifts more than the spatial in-world twin, so the two disagree; c30's o_resync re-synchronised census shadow, run on per-window genotype censuses, would arbitrate; (2) separate spatial local adaptation from a temporal chase (a well-mixed variant); (3) the kinds are new specificities in a relabelling-symmetric interaction, not new functions, and the space is finite (2^20), so a reviewer may call this a Red Queen over an enormous repertoire; larger nb and a dt/size variant would show whether the rate holds; (4) individuals and division are imposed by the agent rules, so I and D are by construction here.
limits: One parameter set (nb = 20, w = 10, u = 0.003 per bit); w = 3 and 6 drive predators extinct (40k-step screens), so the regime is a window, not generic. Six seeds of 200k steps (about 260 predator and 1800 prey generations) and one of 700k. The neutral twin's capture is constant in time; the shuffled twin lowers realised capture to 0.09-0.12 and lost its predators in 2/6 seeds. Analyses use one window and Lc (10000) for the twin comparison. The genotype figures show consensus bits, not the spatial structure of genotypes. Particles, energy budgets and division are agent rules, not emergent bodies.
